title: Delhi to Host Two-Day Diwali Festival With Drone Show at Central Park
excerpt: 'Dilli Ki Diwali' brings a mega drone show, bhajan clubbing and competitions worth up to Rs 1.51 lakh to Connaught Place on November 6 and 7.
body:
• The Delhi government and Delhi Tourism host 'Dilli Ki Diwali – Sabse Nirali, Milkar Manane Wali' at Central Park, Connaught Place, on Friday, November 6 and Saturday, November 7, 2026.
  • A mega drone show and 'Bhajan Clubbing' headline the programme on November 7, alongside cultural performances across both days.
  • Three public competitions — RWA Rangoli, Shoot 'n Shine photography and REEL It — carry cash prizes of up to Rs 1,51,000; entries close at midnight on November 6.
  • The announcement does not state event timings or admission charges — check Delhi Tourism's official channels before you go.

Delhi will celebrate Diwali in the open this year. The Delhi government and Delhi Tourism are staging a two-day public festival, 'Dilli Ki Diwali – Sabse Nirali, Milkar Manane Wali', at Central Park in Connaught Place on November 6 and 7, built around a mega drone show, cultural programmes and competitions with cash prizes.

Plan Your Visit

  • Date: Friday, November 6 – Saturday, November 7, 2026
  • Time: Timings are not stated in the announcement — check Delhi Tourism's official channels before you go.
  • Venue: Central Park, Connaught Place
  • Address: Central Park, Connaught Place, New Delhi 110001
  • Admission: Not stated in the announcement — check with Delhi Tourism before you go.
  • Competitions: Entries for RWA Rangoli, Shoot 'n Shine and REEL It close at midnight (IST) on November 6, 2026.
  • Directions: Get directions

"Plan Your Visit Date: Friday, November 6 – Saturday, November 7, 2026 Time: Timings are not stated in the announcement — check Delhi Tourism's official channels before you go."

What is on

The two days run under the banner 'Jugmug Diwali'. The headline acts are saved for the second evening: a large-scale drone show over Central Park on November 7, paired with 'Bhajan Clubbing' — devotional music presented in a club-style set — alongside cultural programmes across both days. The festival is being held under the leadership of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, with community togetherness as its stated theme.

Three competitions, and the prize money

Delhi Tourism has opened three competitions, all built around themes of eco-friendly celebration, sustainable decor, Delhi's heritage, community spirit and kindness:

  • RWA Rangoli: registered Resident Welfare Associations create rangolis from eco-friendly materials between November 5 and 6. The top Golden Diya Award carries Rs 71,000, with two awards of Rs 41,000, three of Rs 21,000 and 25 special awards of Rs 11,000.
  • Shoot 'n Shine: a photography contest for Diwali moments. The top Golden Frame Award is Rs 1,01,000, with two awards of Rs 51,000 and three of Rs 21,000.
  • REEL It: short-form videos of up to 45 seconds. The top Golden Lens Award is Rs 1,51,000 — the largest individual prize of the festival — with two awards of Rs 1,01,000 and three of Rs 51,000.

Entries for all three competitions close at midnight IST on November 6, 2026 — before the festival's second day begins, so creators need to shoot the opening day or use earlier Diwali material.

Why it matters

Delhi has been scaling up its official Diwali programming, and a Central Park festival puts the celebration in the city's most accessible public space rather than behind ticketed gates. For diaspora families visiting Delhi over the Diwali week, it is the easiest official celebration to walk into — subject to the timings Delhi Tourism has yet to publish.
